summary: Iteration 144: I tested backend/tools/reset_student_data.py (prepare/apply) from start to finish against the dedicated DB tejas_isolated_reset144, using a pure in-memory fake private object store (no real storage PUT, no secrets). I restored the backup into the shadow DB tejas_isolated_restore144. Suite: backend/tests/test_iter144_student_reset.py, 40 cases run serially (-n 0), about 4.5 s per run. Result: 35 passed, 1 failed (a real CLI bug), and 4 strict-xfail tests that pin real defects or gaps. Each strict-xfail fails today as expected and will flip to failing (XPASS) once main fixes the code. Verified: the writers_paused guard on both actions (plus the CLI flag); missing owner fails closed; a role overlap across roots fails; read-back mismatch and any DB change (target or protected) during backup block prepare with no receipt. The plan matches exactly the hand-marked expected targets for include_unlinked=True and False. Covered target shapes: student users, phone profiles, attempts including a retry child, legacy id-only ledgers, orphan ledgers, the 13 unlinked old user IDs, score versions, reviews, reports, saved tests, sessions, preflights, cohort entries and snapshots, grade/report/cohort jobs and audits. Shared AI jobs, content, owner, admin and reviewer records, and unknown foreign collections are kept. Every protected document is canonically byte-identical after apply. Affected cohorts get dirty=true and generation=student-reset-<id>; the owner-only cohort and the owner's cohort entries are untouched. Real tejas.auth.identity (temporarily rebound inside the process to a Motor handle on the test DB, then restored; no JWT changes) raises for the deleted student user and phone profile, and still returns the owner without password_hash. Backup: an 8 MiB chunk split was forced (each non-last tejas_files part decompresses to >= 8 MiB). After restoring every part into the shadow DB, canonical fingerprints of all 160 non-empty documents equal the original: ObjectId, datetimes from 1960 and 2026, Binary subtypes 0/4/5/128, Decimal128 including NaN, Int64 min, Timestamp, Regex, Code with scope, DBRef, MinKey/MaxKey, -0.0/inf/NaN, string and compound _id. Fail-closed with zero deletion and the receipt still 'prepared' for 11 tamper cases: part bit-flip, missing part, missing manifest, count tamper, plan tamper, wrong approval, wrong binding, wrong owner email, a different owner, wrong manifest DB name, unknown reset_id. A new student plus activity created after prepare survives. These all block with nothing deleted: a new retry child, a new session, mutated answers, a mutated legacy ledger, student->reviewer, student->owner, a phone id becoming staff, new activity by an unlinked old user. Concurrency: losing the prepared->applying CAS refuses. A partial crash after 4 delete_many calls leaves phase 'applying'; the resume finishes with the exact expected end state. A complete replay does not delete again. A non-target mutation during apply is detected, and resume is then blocked. HONEST INCIDENT: during my first two runs mongod crashed twice (05:34:06 and 05:34:23 UTC, WT_PANIC 'Too many open files'). Cause: my per-test drop_database/recreate churn, about 30 collections per test, against mongod's 1024 soft fd limit. Supervisor restarted mongod automatically. I rewrote the fixtures to delete_many instead of drop; no fatal errors since. Afterwards: customer DB read-only inventory shows 0 qa144 records, and /api/health returns 200.

critical.issue: `from tejas_storage import upload, request` raises ImportError: tejas_storage has no `upload` (it has put_object(path, data, content_type) -> str path, get_object, request). The real CLI cannot run prepare or apply at all. It fails before any write, so it is safe but non-functional. The put lambda also assumes a dict return {'path': ...}, but put_object returns a str and needs a caller-chosen path. Proven by test_cli_storage_imports_exist.

minor.issue: Orphan attempt IDs are collected from non-staff rows, but the OWNED scope then deletes EVERY row with that attempt_id, including an owner or staff row that shares it. The staff filter applies only at discovery, not at deletion. Repro: an owner review and an anonymous score_version both pointing at attempt 'gone' -> the owner review is deleted, and the protected fingerprint cannot catch it because the row is in the plan. Fix: exclude user_id in staff (or require user_id missing / in users) in the attempt_id branch of OWNED and the jobs scopes. Pinned by strict xfail test_owner_row_sharing_orphan_attempt_id_is_protected.

Apply does not check that the verified backup contains every planned target _id with a matching sha, or that per-collection totals match prepare. If parts are removed from the manifest and the new hash is approved, deletion still goes ahead with an incomplete backup. Recommend: store per-collection counts plus a covered-target digest in the receipt, recompute them during verification, and require that every plan record is found in the parts. Pinned by strict xfail test_manifest_missing_part_for_targets_blocks.

encoded() uses sort_keys=True, so restored BSON loses its original field order: 150 of 160 documents have different raw bytes, while canonical fingerprints still match. Mongo embedded-document equality queries are order-sensitive. Back up with sort_keys=False and keep sorted encoding only for digests. Pinned by strict xfail test_backup_preserves_raw_bson_field_order.

The manifest has no index definitions; the shadow restore only had _id_ (the unique email index was lost). Empty collections are not recorded either. Add list_indexes/options per collection to the manifest. Pinned by strict xfail test_manifest_records_indexes.

Two processes that both see phase 'applying' (resume) can run deletions at the same time; the CAS only guards prepared->applying. Deletion is idempotent, so this is low risk, but consider a lease or owner token on the applying phase.

Student PII stays in collections outside the scope: unknown foreign collections (by design), tejas_phone_limits/login_limits (TTL-hashed), audits where the student is a target rather than the actor, jobs of unlinked users whose attempt link is gone, and ai_solutions.requested_by. These are kept on purpose to fail safe; document them as residual. Phone profiles without a role are not targeted (a test confirms they are kept). The customer DB currently has 0 such profiles (read-only count).

mongod fd soft limit is 1024 (hard 1048576). Repeated collection create/drop pushed WiredTiger into WT_PANIC and crashed mongod twice. Any shadow restore or QA flow that churns collections on this shared mongod can crash every app. Raise the soft ulimit, or never drop/create in a loop.

action_items: Fix CLI storage wiring: use the existing private storage API (put_object with an owner-scoped generated path, returning {'path': path}; fetch through request('GET', path).content or a non-caching get). Then remove the ImportError. Do NOT run it against the customer DB until the load QA passes.
Restrict deletion of rows found only through an orphan attempt_id so it excludes staff/owner user_id rows (OWNED and jobs scopes).
Make apply require that the backup covers every planned target _id with a matching sha, and that per-collection counts match the receipt.
Back up documents with their original key order (no sort_keys) and record index definitions and collection options in the manifest.
Optionally add a lease to the 'applying' phase; document the residual PII collections that are intentionally kept.
Re-run prepare fresh at operation time: the real preview inventory has already moved (now 2 attempts, 15 cohort entries, 9 ledgers, 10 preflights, from real learner activity at 05:30 UTC, not QA).
critical_code_review_comments: Overall design is sound: offline guard, fingerprint of everything outside the target set before and after, prepared->applying CAS, idempotent resume, complete short-circuit, and strict refusal when targets drift or a role is promoted.
public_receipt always reports private_backup_verified=True, which is only honest because it is printed after verification succeeds. owner_and_papers_retained depends only on the phase.
The binding is the sha of MONGO_URL+DB_NAME, so rotating credentials or reformatting the URL makes an approved receipt unusable (fails closed, acceptable; document it).

The writers_paused flag is only an operator acknowledgement; it does not prove the system is quiet. The before/after fingerprints detect writes but do not prevent them. The external stop of web/cron workers remains a required production step.

success_rate.backend: 35/36 non-xfail passed (1 real CLI bug); 4 strict-xfail confirm real gaps

seed_data_creation: Only synthetic qa144-* fixtures inside tejas_isolated_reset144 and tejas_isolated_restore144. Both DBs are dropped at session teardown; after the run they are absent from list_database_names. The customer DB has 0 qa144 records, and its collection set is unchanged (read-only checks).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_iter144_student_reset.py -q -n 0 (MUST use -n 0: pytest.ini enables xdist, and the tests share one isolated DB). Fixtures use delete_many, not drop, to avoid exhausting mongod fds. After main fixes the code, the strict xfails will XPASS: remove the xfail marks. The test file is test-only; the shared iso harness and app code were not modified.
rca of the issue: CLI ImportError: tools/reset_student_data.py imports a non-existent tejas_storage.upload. mongod crash: the QA fixture's drop_database per test created ~60 new WiredTiger files per test; WT keeps dropped idents open until sweep; with the 1024 soft limit, directory-sync open hit EMFILE, leading to WT_PANIC and fassert 50853. Mitigation applied in the test: wipe with delete_many.
